segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Hi.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Great to see you!

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I’m Jody, and I’ll be look after both of you for the first month you’re working here at the Amersham Theatre.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I’ll tell you something about the theatre now, then take you to meet two of the other staff.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It’s an old building, and it’s been modernised several times.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In fact, as you can see, we’re carrying out a major refurbishment at the moment.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The interior has just been repainted, and we’re about to start on the exterior of the building – that’ll be a big job.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The work’s running over budget, so we’ve had to postpone installing an elevator.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I hope you’re happy running up and down stairs!

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: When the theatre was built, people were generally slimmer and shorter than now, and the seats were very close together.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We’ve replaced them with larger seats, with more legroom.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This means fewer seats in total, but we’ve taken the opportunity to install seats that can easily be moved ( & ), to create different acting spaces.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We’ve also turned a few storerooms over to other purposes like using them for meetings. ( & ) We try hard to involve members of the public in the theatre.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: One way is by organising backstage tours so people can be shown round the building and learn how a theatre operates.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: These are proving very popular ( &14).

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: What we’re finding is that people want to have lunch or a cup of coffee while they’re here, so we’re looking into the possibility of opening a café in due course.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We have a bookshop, which specialises in books about drama and that attracts plenty of customers ( & ).

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Then there are two large rooms that will be decorated next month, and they’ll be available for hire, for conferences and private functions, such as parties.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We’re also considering hiring out costumes to amateur drama clubs.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now I want to tell you about our workshops.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We recently started a programme of workshops that anyone can join.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Eventually we intend to run courses in acting, but we’re waiting until we’ve got the right people in place as trainers.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: That’s proving more difficult than we’d expected!

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There’s a big demand to learn about the technical side of putting on a production, and our lighting workshop has already started with great success ( & ).

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We’re going to start one on sound next month.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: A number of people have enquired about workshops on make-up, and that’s something we’re considering for the future.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: A surprise success is the workshop on making puppets – we happen to have someone working here who does it as a hobby, and she offered to run a workshop.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It was so popular we’re now running them every month! ( & ) Now, a word about the layout of the building.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The auditorium, stage and dressing rooms for the actors are all below ground level.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Here on the ground floor we have most of the rooms that the public doesn’t see.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The majority are internal, so they have windows in the roof to light them.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Standing here in the foyer, you’re probably wondering why the box office isn’t here, where the public would expect to find it.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Well, you might have noticed it on your way in – although it’s part of this building, it’s next door with a separate entrance from the road. For the theatre manager’s office, you go across the foyer and through the double doors, turn right, and it’s the room at the end of the corridor, with the door on the left. The lighting box is where the computerised stage lighting is operated and it’s at the back of the building.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: When you’re through the double doors turn left, turn right at the water cooler, and right again at the end.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It’s the second room along that corridor.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The lighting box has a window into the auditorium, which of course is below us.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The artistic director’s office is through the double doors, turn right and it’s the first room you come to on the right-hand side.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And finally, for the moment, the room where I’ll take you next – the relaxation room.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So if you’d like to come with me ...
